chapter_title: Data Structures, Algorithms, Database & Operating Systems

topics.title: ADT & Asymptotic Analysis
topics.content:
Data Structures & ADT:
- Data Type: Kind of data (integer, float)[cite: 1].
- Abstract Data Type (ADT): Logical description/blueprint defining organization and operations independent of implementation (e.g., Stack ADT implemented via array or linked list)[cite: 1].

Asymptotic Notations (BTO):
- Big O ($O$): Upper bound; worst-case complexity[cite: 1].
- Theta ($\Theta$): Tight bound; average-case complexity[cite: 1].
- Omega ($\Omega$): Lower bound; best-case complexity[cite: 1].
- Time Growth Hierarchy: $O(1) < O(\log n) < O(n) < O(n \log n) < O(n^2) < O(2^n)$[cite: 1].

topics.title: Stack & Queue Data Structures
topics.content:
Stack (LIFO):
- Operations: Push, Pop, Peek/Top, isEmpty[cite: 1].
- Applications: Recursion, function calls, Infix-to-Postfix conversion, Postfix evaluation[cite: 1].
- Precedence Rule: Higher/equal precedence operators on stack pop before lower ones; parentheses enforce scope[cite: 1].

Queue (FIFO):
- Operations: Enqueue (at rear), Dequeue (from front)[cite: 1].
- Types: Simple Queue, Circular Queue (prevents wasted space), Priority Queue (elements processed by priority)[cite: 1].

topics.title: Linked Lists & Trees
topics.content:
Linked Lists:
- Dynamic size memory allocation[cite: 1].
- Types: Singly (data + next pointer), Doubly (next + previous pointers), Circular (last node points to root/first)[cite: 1].
- Head Insertion Complexity: $O(1)$[cite: 1].

Trees & Traversals:
- Binary Tree: Maximum of 2 children per node[cite: 1].
- Traversals: Inorder (Left-Root-Right; gives sorted sequence for BST), Preorder (Root-Left-Right; used to copy tree), Postorder (Left-Right-Root; used to delete tree)[cite: 1].
- Binary Search Tree (BST): Left child < Parent < Right child[cite: 1].
- AVL Tree: Self-balancing BST where height difference between subtrees $|BF| \le 1$; guarantees $O(\log n)$ operations[cite: 1].

topics.title: Sorting Algorithms
topics.content:
Internal vs. External Sorting:
- Internal: All data fits in RAM (e.g., Quick, Insertion, Heap)[cite: 1].
- External: Data resides on disk due to memory limits (e.g., External Merge Sort)[cite: 1].

Algorithm Complexities & Features:
- Insertion Sort: Best $O(n)$, Worst $O(n^2)$, Stable, In-place; optimal for nearly sorted data[cite: 1].
- Selection Sort: Always $O(n^2)$, Unstable, In-place[cite: 1].
- Bubble Sort: Best $O(n)$, Worst $O(n^2)$, Stable, In-place[cite: 1].
- Merge Sort: Always $O(n \log n)$, Stable, Divide-and-Conquer; requires $O(n)$ extra space[cite: 1].
- Quick Sort: Average $O(n \log n)$, Worst $O(n^2)$ (bad pivot selection), Unstable, In-place[cite: 1].
- Heap Sort: Always $O(n \log n)$, Unstable, In-place[cite: 1].
- Radix Sort: Time $O(d \times n)$, Non-comparison digit-based sort[cite: 1].

topics.title: Searching & Hashing
topics.content:
Searching:
- Linear Search: $O(n)$ time; works on unsorted lists[cite: 1].
- Binary Search: $O(\log n)$ time; requires sorted arrays[cite: 1].

Hashing:
- Hash Function: Maps key to table index ($h(k) = k \bmod m$)[cite: 1]. Ideal search time $O(1)$[cite: 1].
- Collisions: Occur when two distinct keys hash to the same index[cite: 1].
- Collision Resolution: Separate Chaining (linked lists) vs Open Addressing (Linear Probing, Quadratic Probing, Double Hashing)[cite: 1].

topics.title: Graphs & Graph Algorithms
topics.content:
Graph Representations:
- Adjacency Matrix: $O(V^2)$ space; preferred for dense graphs[cite: 1].
- Adjacency List: $O(V + E)$ space; preferred for sparse graphs[cite: 1].

Graph Algorithms:
- Traversals: BFS uses Queue (level-by-level, shortest path in unweighted graph); DFS uses Stack/Recursion (deep exploration, topological sort)[cite: 1].
- Topological Sorting: Linear ordering for Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAG)[cite: 1].
- Minimum Spanning Tree (MST): Prim's ($O(E \log V)$, node-greedy) and Kruskal's ($O(E \log E)$, edge-sorting with Union-Find)[cite: 1].
- Shortest Path: Dijkstra's algorithm ($O(E \log V)$ greedy; fails for negative edge weights)[cite: 1].
- Transitive Closure: Warshall's Algorithm ($O(V^3)$ dynamic programming)[cite: 1].

topics.title: Database Architecture & E-R Model
topics.content:
Data Abstraction Levels:
- Physical Level (how stored), Logical Level (what stored/tables), View Level (user schema)[cite: 1]. Data Independence decouples schema layers[cite: 1].

E-R Concepts:
- Entities: Strong (independent primary key) vs Weak (depends on strong entity)[cite: 1].
- Attributes: Simple, Composite, Single-valued, Multi-valued (double oval), Derived (dashed oval)[cite: 1].
- Keys: Primary Key (unique, non-NULL), Candidate Key, Foreign Key (referential integrity), Composite Key[cite: 1].

topics.title: Normalization & Relational Algebra/SQL
topics.content:
Normalization Forms:
- 1NF: Atomic values, no repeating groups[cite: 1].
- 2NF: In 1NF + eliminates partial dependencies (non-key attributes depend on whole primary key)[cite: 1].
- 3NF: In 2NF + eliminates transitive dependencies (non-key $\rightarrow$ non-key)[cite: 1].
- BCNF: Stricter 3NF; for every $A \rightarrow B$, $A$ must be a superkey[cite: 1].

SQL Categories & Relational Algebra:
- DDL: CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE[cite: 1].
- DML: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE[cite: 1].
- Relational Algebra: Select ($\sigma$), Project ($\pi$), Union ($\cup$), Join ($\bowtie$)[cite: 1].
- View: Virtual table providing security/simplification without storing physical data[cite: 1].

topics.title: ACID Properties & Concurrency Control
topics.content:
ACID Properties:
- Atomicity (all or nothing), Consistency (valid state), Isolation (independent concurrent execution), Durability (permanent changes)[cite: 1].

Concurrency & Lock-Based Protocols:
- Anomalies: Dirty Read (reading uncommitted data), Lost Update, Unrepeatable Read, Phantom Read[cite: 1].
- Locking: Shared Lock (S, read-only) vs Exclusive Lock (X, read/write)[cite: 1].
- Two-Phase Locking (2PL): Growing phase (acquire locks) followed by Shrinking phase (release locks); guarantees serializability[cite: 1].

topics.title: Deadlocks & Crash Recovery
topics.content:
Deadlock Handling:
- Detection: Uses Wait-for Graphs (cycles indicate deadlocks)[cite: 1].
- Prevention: Ensures at least one deadlock condition cannot hold (e.g., resource ordering)[cite: 1].

Crash Recovery:
- Log-Based Recovery: Uses Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) where log records are written to disk prior to data writes[cite: 1].
- UNDO uses old values (rollback); REDO uses new values (reapply)[cite: 1]. Checkpoints minimize log scanning time during recovery[cite: 1].

topics.title: OS Architecture & Process Management
topics.content:
OS Architecture:
- Monolithic vs Microkernel (minimal kernel, services run in user space for high reliability)[cite: 1].

Processes vs Threads:
- Process: Program in execution with independent PCB and memory space[cite: 1]. States: New, Ready, Running, Blocked/Waiting, Terminated[cite: 1]. Context Switching saves/restores process states[cite: 1].
- Thread: Lightweight execution unit within a process; shares code/memory space[cite: 1]. Kernel-level threads execute independently of main process[cite: 1].

CPU Scheduling:
- Non-Preemptive: FCFS (convoy effect), SJF (optimal average wait time, can cause starvation)[cite: 1].
- Preemptive: Round Robin (uses time quantum/slice), SRTF (preemptive SJF)[cite: 1].

topics.title: Process Synchronization
topics.content:
Concepts & Criteria:
- Race Condition: Unpredictable outcome dependent on execution order[cite: 1].
- Critical Section Requirements: Mutual Exclusion, Progress, Bounded Waiting[cite: 1].

Primitives:
- Mutex: Binary lock providing mutual exclusion[cite: 1].
- Semaphore: Integer variable operated via wait ($P$) and signal ($V$) primitives[cite: 1]. Counting semaphore manages arbitrary resource quantities[cite: 1].
- Monitor: High-level language construct providing automatic mutual exclusion[cite: 1].

topics.title: Memory Management & Virtual Memory
topics.content:
Address Binding & Allocation:
- MMU translates CPU logical addresses to physical RAM addresses[cite: 1]. Placement strategies: First Fit, Best Fit (minimizes remaining space), Worst Fit[cite: 1].

Virtual Memory & Paging:
- Paging divides logical memory into Pages and physical memory into Frames; managed via Page Tables[cite: 1]. Eliminates external fragmentation[cite: 1].
- Demand Paging: Pages loaded only when referenced; causes Page Fault if page is missing from RAM[cite: 1].
- Replacement Algorithms: FIFO (suffers from Belady's Anomaly), Optimal (OPT - lowest fault rate, theoretical benchmark), LRU (Least Recently Used)[cite: 1].
- Thrashing: System spends more time swapping pages than executing instructions due to high multiprogramming[cite: 1].

topics.title: File Systems & Disk Scheduling
topics.content:
File Allocation Methods:
- Contiguous: Fast sequential/random access, suffers heavily from external fragmentation[cite: 1].
- Linked: Pointer chain per block; no external fragmentation, poor random access[cite: 1].
- Indexed: Index block holds pointers (e.g., UNIX inodes hold file metadata/block addresses)[cite: 1].

Disk Scheduling Algorithms:
- FCFS, SSTF (Shortest Seek Time First), SCAN (elevator algorithm), C-SCAN (circular scan in one direction only), LOOK/C-LOOK[cite: 1].

questions.question: What does Big-O notation describe in algorithm analysis?
questions.explanation: Big O notation specifies the asymptotic upper bound, representing the worst-case time complexity of an algorithm[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which data structure is fundamentally used for converting infix expressions to postfix format?
questions.explanation: Stacks store operators and evaluate operator precedence during infix-to-postfix conversion[cite: 1].

questions.question: What is the result of evaluating the postfix expression: 5 3 + 2 * ?
questions.explanation: Evaluation: 5 + 3 = 8, followed by 8 * 2 = 16[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which data structure follows the First-In First-Out (FIFO) principle?
questions.explanation: Queues process elements in arrival order, adhering to FIFO[cite: 1].

questions.question: In a Doubly Linked List, each node contains how many pointer fields?
questions.explanation: Each node in a doubly linked list holds pointers to both the next and previous nodes[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which tree traversal order visits the root node first, followed by the left and right subtrees?
questions.explanation: Preorder traversal order is Root-Left-Right[cite: 1].

questions.question: In a Binary Search Tree (BST), which traversal produces elements in sorted ascending order?
questions.explanation: Inorder traversal (Left-Root-Right) visits BST nodes in non-decreasing sorted order[cite: 1].

questions.question: What is the maximum allowed height difference (balance factor) between left and right subtrees in an AVL tree?
questions.explanation: AVL trees strictly balance subtrees such that $|h_L - h_R| \le 1$[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which tree traversal algorithm is standard for deleting/deallocating an entire binary tree?
questions.explanation: Postorder deletes children subtrees prior to deleting the parent root node[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm exhibits a worst-case time complexity of O(n^2) due to poor pivot selection?
questions.explanation: Quick Sort degrades to $O(n^2)$ time when partition pivots are consistently unbalanced[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which of the following sorting algorithms is NOT comparison-based?
questions.explanation: Radix Sort processes keys digit by digit rather than using pairwise element comparisons[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm guarantees O(n log n) time complexity in all cases while preserving stability?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort consistently operates in $O(n \log n)$ time and maintains relative ordering of equal keys[cite: 1].

questions.question: What is a major requirement for running a Binary Search on an array?
options: The array must be dynamically allocated
The array size must be a power of 2
The array must contain positive values
questions.explanation: Binary search relies on sorted order to divide the search space systematically[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which collision resolution strategy handles hash table collisions by creating linked lists at indices?
questions.explanation: Separate chaining resolves index collisions by attaching dynamic linked lists[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which graph traversal implementation relies on a Queue data structure?
questions.explanation: BFS uses a Queue to explore adjacent vertices level-by-level[cite: 1].

questions.question: Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm fails or produces incorrect results under which condition?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's greedy choice property assumes non-negative edge weights[cite: 1].

questions.question: What is the time complexity of Warshall's algorithm for finding transitive closure?
questions.explanation: Warshall's dynamic programming matrix algorithm runs in $O(V^3)$ time[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which schema abstraction level describes HOW data is physically stored on disk blocks?
questions.explanation: The physical level details low-level storage structures, paths, and file formats[cite: 1].

questions.question: An attribute calculated dynamically from other existing database fields (e.g., Age from DOB) is a:
questions.explanation: Derived attributes are computed dynamically from stored base attributes[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which normal form specifically removes partial functional dependencies?
questions.explanation: 2NF eliminates partial dependencies by ensuring all non-key attributes depend on the full primary key[cite: 1].

questions.question: Removing transitive dependencies (non-key attribute determining another non-key attribute) achieves:
questions.explanation: 3NF eliminates transitive dependencies between non-prime attributes[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which of the following SQL commands belongs to the Data Manipulation Language (DML)?
questions.explanation: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE are DML commands[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which relational algebra operator filters specific rows based on a given condition?
questions.explanation: Select ($\sigma$) filters tuple rows satisfying logical predicate conditions[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which ACID property guarantees that all transaction operations execute completely or none do?
questions.explanation: Atomicity enforces the 'all-or-nothing' execution rule for transactions[cite: 1].

questions.question: Reading uncommitted data modified by another concurrent transaction is known as a:
questions.explanation: A dirty read occurs when a transaction reads uncommitted changes[cite: 1].

questions.question: What log management rule requires log records to be written to disk prior to modified database blocks?
questions.explanation: Write-Ahead Logging ensures undo/redo log entries hit stable storage before updated database pages[cite: 1].

questions.question: In Operating Systems, a situation where outcome depends unpredictably on process execution order is called a:
questions.explanation: Race conditions produce non-deterministic results based on thread scheduling timing[cite: 1].

questions.question: Which CPU scheduling algorithm gives the lowest theoretical average waiting time for a set of jobs?
questions.explanation: SJF scheduling minimizes overall average waiting time[cite: 1].

questions.question: An anomaly where adding more physical page frames increases total page faults under FIFO is called:
questions.explanation: Belady's Anomaly demonstrates that increasing page frames under FIFO can increase page fault occurrences[cite: 1].

questions.question: In UNIX file systems, what structure stores file metadata, including permissions, size, and block pointers?
questions.explanation: UNIX inodes hold essential metadata and disk block indexing pointers for files[cite: 1].
